issue.title: Add a shell: filter token (shell:gate, shell:proc) to sase agent search
issue.description:
Give `sase agent search` (and the ACE Artifacts Agent pane, which shares the profile) a
`shell:` filter token — `shell:gate`, `shell:proc` — so a family shell can be selected by
its kind rather than by string-parsing a member suffix.

Proposed by phase bead sase-ud.8 (gate-fork-cli) while landing epic sase-ud, which risk
R6 required to check whether `sase agent search` needs a `shell:gate` token and either
handle it or file a task. sase-ud.8 verified the shape of the work rather than doing it:

- The `agent_artifacts` SQLite table (sase-core `crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/index.rs`,
  CREATE TABLE around line 1982) has no `shell_kind` / `agent_family_role` / `gate_id`
  column. Those fields live only in the `record_json` blob, which the Python catalog
  deliberately never reads (`src/sase/agents/catalog/_sources.py`: "Only the columns the
  catalog's kind/attribute derivation actually needs. Never SELECT *").
- A real token therefore needs sase-core to add a `shell_kind` column via
  `ensure_agent_artifacts_column`, populate it on INSERT, bump the index schema version,
  and rebuild bindings; then, in this repo, `agents/catalog/_sources.py`
  (`_ARTIFACT_INDEX_COLUMNS` + `ArtifactIndexRecord`), `_models.py` (`AgentCatalogRow`),
  `_build.py` (`_build_row`), `_query.py` (`agent_catalog_query_entry`), and
  `ace/query_profile/profiles/_agents.py` (`QueryFieldSpec`) all need additions.

First decide whether the column is worth it: `role:gate` already works today with zero
code changes, because `role` is derived by string-parsing the member suffix
(`acme--gate` -> `role=gate`). That may be sufficient, in which case the right outcome is
documenting `role:` as the supported spelling instead of adding a cross-repo column.

task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
Epic sase-ud shipped gate shells as a third family-shell kind; naming a shell kind in a
query is a search/catalog capability, not gate-shell behavior. The work lands in the
sase-core agent-scan index and the agents query profile — surfaces epic sase-ud never
touched — and needs a Rust schema bump plus a binding rebuild, so it could not ride along
with the epic.

payload.description: sase-tj owns 'sase agent search' (phase sase-tj.8) and the agents query profile this token would extend
